data.why: There is no file-upload path in this app; the only input is a 7-field form pre-filled with a real TOI's catalog measurements, and the frozen model artifact is already bundled in the repo at artifacts/exoscout_v0_5.joblib.

goals: Classify a specific TESS Object of Interest's catalog measurements as planet-like or a false positive and read off the model's uncalibrated score against the frozen threshold.
Test how the classification changes when one or more measurements are missing by clearing a field and observing the pipeline's median imputation and missingness-indicator behavior.
Probe the decision boundary by perturbing a single feature (e.g. shrinking transit depth or shortening transit duration) and watching the score cross the 0.5 threshold.

Sanity-check the model against known catalog dispositions by entering values resembling a textbook false positive (e.g. very shallow, V-shaped-like depth/duration combination) versus a confident planet.
Relate the classification to the feature-importance story in docs/METHODOLOGY.md, confirming that transit geometry (period, duration, depth) dominates over stellar properties.

review.summary: The tree gets this single-form classifier right: it frames ExoScout as one-candidate vetting plus probing of the model, it covers the score, threshold, missing-data and validation behaviour, and every screen I checked matches its node, with honest not_done notes. Before filing it needs light restructuring (misplaced t9, wrong branch on t7, phase 5 repeating phase 3's method), a task for entering a new candidate's own measurements, and f3 marked as a usage pattern, not a component.
